title: A nonzero polynomial relation lowers the dimension of a quasi-finite polynomial algebra
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $n\ge0$ be an integer, and let $T$ be a commutative finite type $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Let $\varphi:k[t_1,\dots,t_n]\to T$ be a $k$-algebra homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] which is of finite type and quasi-finite at every prime of $T$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]. If $\ker\varphi$ contains a nonzero polynomial, then $\dim\operatorname{Spec}T<n$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. The zero ring is permitted, with empty spectrum of dimension $-\infty$.

source.place: Tag 00QK (lemma-finite-type-domain-over-valuation-ring-dim-fibres), proof, last sentence: the nonzero residue-polynomial kernel implies the strict dimension bound; a general field-algebra input behind that inference.

proof.text: If $T=0$, its spectrum is empty and has dimension $-\infty<n$, as in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Hence assume $T\ne0$. If $n=0$, the polynomial ring is $k$ and a nonzero element of the kernel is a unit: applying $\varphi$ to its inverse times itself gives $1_T=0$, a contradiction. Thus it remains to treat $n\ge1$.

source.place: Tag 00QK (lemma-finite-type-domain-over-valuation-ring-dim-fibres), final inference; empty and zero-variable cases made explicit

proof.text: Put $P=k[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$. The field $k$ is Noetherian because its only ideals are $(0)$ and $k$, and has dimension zero because its sole prime ideal is $(0)$. Apply [lem-sf-noetherian-polynomial-dimension] to get $\dim P=n$. Also $P$ is a domain directly from the polynomial multiplication [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]: order exponent vectors lexicographically; in a nonzero polynomial choose the largest exponent in its finite support. For two nonzero polynomials with largest exponents $a,b$, the largest exponent of their product is $a+b$, with coefficient the product of their nonzero leading coefficients. This coefficient is nonzero in the field. Thus $(0)$ is a prime ideal of $P$.

source.place: Tag 00QG (lemma-dimension-quasi-finite-over-polynomial-algebra), polynomial-source dimension input, with the Noetherian polynomial dimension theorem; domain verification from multiplication

proof.text: Let $I=\ker\varphi$, choose $0\ne h\in I$, and put $R=P/I$. The formula $\psi(p+I)=\varphi(p)$ is well defined because $I$ is the kernel, and factors $\varphi$ through $R$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-finite-four-rings] to $P\to T$, $P\to R$, $R\xrightarrow{\psi}T$ and $T\xrightarrow{1}T$. The square commutes. Its finite-sum hypothesis holds because each $t\in T$ is the single product $t\cdot1$, with the first factor in the image of $T\xrightarrow{1}T$ and the second in the image of $R$. For each prime $\mathfrak q$ of the bottom $T$, its inverse image in the top $T$ is the same $\mathfrak q$, where the original map is quasi-finite by hypothesis. The cited statement therefore gives that $\psi:R\to T$ is finite type and quasi-finite at every prime of $T$.

source.place: Tag 00PN (lemma-four-rings), specialized to the quotient of the polynomial source by its kernel

proof.text: Every strict prime chain $\mathfrak r_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak r_\ell$ of $R$ pulls back to a strict prime chain $\widetilde{\mathfrak r}_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\widetilde{\mathfrak r}_\ell$ of $P$ containing $I$. Primality follows by testing products modulo $I$; strictness follows by lifting an element in each successive ideal difference along the surjection $P\to R$. Each lifted ideal contains $h\ne0$, so prepending the prime $(0)$ makes a chain of length $\ell+1$ in $P$. By $\dim P=n$ and the prime-chain definition [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring], $\ell+1\le n$. Thus every prime chain of $R$ has length at most $n-1$.

source.place: Tag 00QK (lemma-finite-type-domain-over-valuation-ring-dim-fibres), final strict dimension inference: explicit prime-chain argument for the nonzero kernel quotient

proof.text: Fix a prime $\mathfrak q$ of $T$ and put $\mathfrak r=\psi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. The localization/chain formula [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime] applied to $R,\mathfrak r$, together with step 4, gives $\dim R_{\mathfrak r}\le n-1$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-inequality-quasi-finite] to $\psi$ at $\mathfrak q$: step 3 verified precisely its finite-type and quasi-finiteness hypotheses. It gives $\dim T_{\mathfrak q}\le\dim R_{\mathfrak r}\le n-1$.

source.place: Tag 00QF (lemma-dimension-inequality-quasi-finite), applied to the kernel quotient source

proof.text: For any strict prime chain of length $\ell$ in $T$, let $\mathfrak q$ be its last prime. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime], $\ell\le\dim T_{\mathfrak q}\le n-1$ by step 5. Taking the supremum of all chain lengths [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] gives $\dim T\le n-1<n$. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-spec-topological-krull-dimension-ring] identifies this ring dimension with $\dim\operatorname{Spec}T$, the dimension in the conclusion.

source.place: Tag 00QK (lemma-finite-type-domain-over-valuation-ring-dim-fibres), final strict inequality, and Tag 00QG concluding passage from local to global dimension
